mainTopic: Protective fences against sin (שבת 13a): reading by lamplight on שבת, a זב eating with a זבה or with an עם הארץ, and whether a נדה may sleep in the same bed as her husband while both are clothed.
overview: This amud continues the משנה's rule against reading by lamplight on שבת. A ברייתא about schoolchildren reading by lamplight is answered in two ways: they read only briefly, or their fear of their teacher keeps them from tilting the lamp. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a זב may not eat with a זבה, so they do not grow used to sin. It also discusses why a careful זב may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ, and אביי and רבא give different reasons. Next the גמרא asks whether a נדה may sleep in one bed with her husband while both are clothed. Several proofs are pushed off using the idea of two minds (דיעות) plus a noticeable change (שינוי). A פסוק in יחזקאל finally settles that it is forbidden. The גמרא notes that רבי פדת disagrees, and that עולא's practice of kissing his sisters clashes with his own strict teaching. Finally, a story begins about a great student who died young, and his widow challenges the תורה's promise of long life. Her words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge: Schoolchildren read by lamplight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ban on reading by lamplight, using a ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says schoolchildren read by lamplight.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that schoolchildren would arrange their sections and read by the light of the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to allow reading by lamplight on שבת. This contradicts our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says you may not read by lamplight on שבת, because you might tilt the lamp to make it burn better. This ברייתא describes children doing exactly that kind of reading, which suggests it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of the lamp

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
the schoolchildren
phrases.notes: Literally 'the children of the house of their teacher.'

phrases.english: would arrange the sections
phrases.notes: They prepared the sections they would learn.

phrases.english: and read by the light of the lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule (discussed on the previous amud) that one may not read by lamplight on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on reading by lamplight on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows children reading by lamplight, which suggests the activity is allowed.

steps.title: First answer: They only read the beginnings of sections
steps.stepSummary: The children only read the opening words of each section, a short amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: they only read the beginnings of the sections.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The children did not read for a long time. They only looked at the first lines of each section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about tilting the lamp comes from reading for a long time. Glancing at a few opening words is too short for that worry, so the ברייתא does not contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you wish, say —
the beginnings of its sections,
phrases.notes: They only read the openings, which takes very little time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by limiting what kind of reading the ברייתא describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The children were reading the whole text by lamplight.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only read the short openings, so there is no real worry that they will tilt the lamp.

steps.title: Second answer: Children fear their teacher
steps.stepSummary: Children are different, because fear of their teacher stops them from touching the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: children are different. Since they are afraid of their teacher, they will not come to tilt the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer. Even if the children read fully, they would not tilt the lamp, because they are afraid of their רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's גזירה exists because an adult might absent-mindedly fix the lamp. Children sitting before their teacher are too afraid to do anything except learn, so the worry does not apply to them.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on reading by lamplight still stands. The ברייתא is explained either as very short reading or as children whose fear of their teacher keeps them from tilting the lamp.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say —
children are different,
since the fear of their teacher is upon them,
they will not come to tilt the lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Children would face the same risk of tilting the lamp as anyone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: Children's fear of their teacher removes the worry, so their case is an exception to the גזירה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: A זב may not eat with a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which compares a similar decree about a זב and a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to it: a זב may not eat (with a זבה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. Like the lamp decree, there is a safeguard that a זב may not eat together with a זבה. This step sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection is the idea of a protective fence. Just as we fear someone will tilt the lamp, we fear that eating together will lead a husband and wife who are both impure to forbidden closeness.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is impure because of a certain bodily discharge
A woman with a similar impurity (forbidden to her husband)

phrases.english: Similar to it, the zav may not eat (with the zava).
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. The full line is 'with the זבה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the lamp discussion and quotes the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב may not eat together with a זבה.

steps.title: How widely purity was kept in Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר notes that the משנה did not even need to forbid a pure person eating with an impure one, because everyone kept purity. The decree was only for two impure people, and it was to prevent sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Come and see how far purity spread in Israel. We did not learn 'a pure man may not eat with an impure woman.' Instead we learned 'a זב may not eat with a זבה,' because it may lead to sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא praises the Jewish people's care for טהרה. The משנה only needed to warn about two impure people eating together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pure person would never eat with an impure one, because that would make him impure. That was so obvious that no rule was needed. A זב and a זבה are both already impure, so impurity is not the concern. The concern is that closeness at meals will lead to forbidden relations.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Come and see
how far purity spread in Israel,
for we did not learn
'the pure man may not eat with the impure woman,'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לֹא יֹאכַל הַזָּב עִם הַזָּבָה
phrases.english: rather, 'the zav may not eat with the zava'
because of becoming accustomed to sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the reason behind the משנה's line in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זב and זבה rule exists to prevent sin, not impurity. Mixing pure and impure people did not even need a rule.

steps.title: A careful זב may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a similar rule: a זב who is careful about purity may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ, in case the עם הארץ draws him close.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to it: a careful זב may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ, in case he makes him used to being with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second example of the same idea. Even when both are impure, a careful person should not share meals with a careless one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men are already impure, so the concern is not simple impurity. The stated reason, 'in case he makes him used to him,' is vague. The גמרא will question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates himself (careful about purity and מעשרות)
An unlearned person, not careful about purity and tithes
He will make him used to being with him

phrases.english: Similar to it:
a zav who is careful (about purity) may not eat
with a zav who is an am ha'aretz,
lest he make him accustomed to (being with) him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ: לֹא יֹאכַל זָב פָּרוּשׁ עִם זָב עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel safeguard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A careful זב may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ.

steps.title: What is wrong with getting used to him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what harm there is in the careful זב becoming friendly with the עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he makes him used to being with him, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason given in the ברייתא. Being friends with someone is not a sin in itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a זב and a זבה, closeness can lead to forbidden relations. Two men becoming friendly has no obvious sin attached, so the ברייתא must explain what the real danger is.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What is the problem?

phrases.english: And if he makes him accustomed to (being with) him,
what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason given at the end of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reason: 'in case he makes him used to him.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Friendship alone is not a sin, so the stated reason does not explain the ban.

steps.title: Correction: He might feed him impure food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: the worry is that the עם הארץ will feed him impure food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: in case he feeds him impure things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the ברייתא's wording. The real danger is that the עם הארץ will serve the careful man impure food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' signals that the old reading is being replaced. Now the danger is a real halachic problem, impure food, and not just friendship.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
lest he feed him impure things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The danger is being fed impure food.

steps.title: But a זב already eats impure food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the correction: a זב is impure, so everything he eats becomes impure anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say a careful זב does not eat impure things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. A זב makes his own food impure by touching it, so being served impure food changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason from step 8 does not work for someone who is already a זב. Whatever he touches becomes impure, so impure food is no new loss for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Is that to say that a careful zav
does not eat impure things?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ זָב פָּרוּשׁ לָאו דְּבָרִים טְמֵאִין אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected reason from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the עם הארץ might feed him impure food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זב makes all his food impure himself, so impure food from the עם הארץ adds no harm.

steps.title: אביי: He might feed him untithed food
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the decree is out of fear that the עם הארץ will feed him food that has not been tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree, in case he feeds him things that are not properly prepared (untithed).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new reason. The danger is not impurity but מעשרות: an עם הארץ might serve food that was never tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a זב does not make untithed food permitted, so this danger is real even for him. That is why the חכמים made a גזירה against eating together.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree lest he feed him
things that are not prepared (untithed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9 with a different danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The danger was impure food, which does not matter to a זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The danger is untithed food, which is forbidden even to a זב.

steps.title: רבא: The habit will carry over to his days of purity
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's reason, since most עמי הארץ do tithe. The danger is that the friendship will continue after the careful man becomes pure, and then the עם הארץ will feed him impure food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Most עמי הארץ do tithe. Rather, the worry is that he will become used to being with him and will feed him impure things in the days of his purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. Untithed food is not a real worry, but the friendship formed now could lead to eating impure food later, once the careful man is pure again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumes most unlearned people do separate מעשרות, so אביי's fear is unlikely. He goes back to the ברייתא's idea of 'getting used to him,' but adds a time element. The real harm happens later, when the careful man is pure and impure food would actually damage him.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, an אמורא who often argues with אביי
In the days of his purity

steps.whatToRemember: A careful זב may not eat with a זב who is an עם הארץ. אביי says the reason is untithed food. רבא says the friendship may lead to eating impure food after he becomes pure.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back the problem of 'getting used to him.' He is explaining why that habit matters: its harm shows up later, in the days of purity.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
most amei ha'aretz do tithe,
rather, lest he become accustomed to (being with) him
and he will feed him impure things
in the days of his purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with אביי's answer in step 10 and offers another answer to step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was untithed food (אביי), or impure food while he is still a זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is impure food later, after he becomes pure, through a friendship formed now.

steps.title: May a נדה sleep in her husband's bed while both are clothed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a נדה may sleep in the same bed as her husband if each is dressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What about a נדה? May she sleep with her husband, she in her clothes and he in his clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question on the same theme of safeguards. It asks whether wearing clothes is enough of a fence, or whether sharing a bed is forbidden entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a נדה are forbidden. The question is whether we need a fence against even being close in one bed when there is a barrier of clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (a real halachic question)
A menstruating woman, forbidden to her husband

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
a niddah, may she sleep with her husband
she in her clothing and he in his clothing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question related to the theme of safeguards against sin.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נדה and her husband may share a bed if both are clothed.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof: Chicken and cheese on one table
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tries to answer from the משנה where בית הלל forbid even placing chicken and cheese on the same table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: Chicken may be served on the table with cheese but not eaten with it, according to בית שמאי. בית הלל say: It may not be served and may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a proof. בית הלל forbid even putting the two foods together, in case they get eaten together, so a נדה and her husband should not share a bed either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha follows בית הלל, who build a fence even against being near something forbidden. The comparison: just as chicken and cheese may not even be placed together, husband and wife should not even be together in bed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is brought up onto the table
The school of הלל (the halacha follows them)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said, come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹף עוֹלֶה עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן
phrases.english: fowl may be placed with cheese on the table
but it is not eaten (with it), the words of Beit Shammai.
Beit Hillel say:
it is neither placed nor eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדה may not sleep with her husband even when both are clothed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which בית הלל forbid even placing chicken and cheese on one table.

steps.title: Rejection: There, only one mind is involved
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: with chicken and cheese only one person is there to forget, but in a bed there are two people to remind each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because there are not (two) minds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's proof. The two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a table, one person alone might forget and eat both foods. In a bed there are two people, and each can remind the other, so the danger is smaller. The question in step 12 is not decided yet; step 23 settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: Minds (separate people who can remind each other)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not permit sharing a bed. It only shows that the chicken-and-cheese case cannot prove the answer either way.

phrases.english: It is different there
for there are not (two) minds.
phrases.notes: At a table there is one person. In a bed there are two who can remind each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. It does not decide the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases differ: one person can forget alone, while two people remind each other.

steps.title: Support from two guests eating meat and cheese at one table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the idea that two minds make a difference. It cites רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows two guests to eat meat and cheese at one table.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that where there are two minds, the case is different. The end of that משנה teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says two guests may eat at one table, one eating meat and one eating cheese, and we are not worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support to the last step's point: when two people are present, they watch out for each other. It brings a case where two people may eat meat and cheese at the same table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one person, chicken and cheese on one table is forbidden, because he might forget. With two guests it is allowed, because each one reminds the other. So two minds really do make things safer, and this would seem to allow the dressed couple in one bed.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. This introduces support for the previous idea.
Minds or awarenesses. Here it means two separate people who can remind each other.
Guests or travelers staying at an inn

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable
that where there are two minds, it is different.
As the latter clause teaches:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָיִים אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Two guests may eat at one table,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְזֶה אוֹכֵל גְּבִינָה,
phrases.english: this one eating meat and this one eating cheese,
and we are not concerned.
phrases.notes: Two people will remind each other not to mix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of step 14, which said two people remind each other.
steps.raayaObject: Two minds make a case safer, so the dressed couple may share a bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows two guests to eat meat and cheese at one table.

steps.title: שמואל limits the guest ruling to strangers
steps.stepSummary: The support is rejected. שמואל taught that the leniency applies only to strangers, and a husband and wife know each other well.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this: רב חנין בר אמי said in the name of שמואל, they only taught this when the guests do not know each other. If they know each other, they are forbidden. And these, husband and wife, certainly know each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 15. The guest leniency only works for strangers, and a married couple is the opposite of strangers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who are close might share food with each other and end up mixing meat and cheese. A husband and wife are very close, so having two minds would not protect them. The guest case now seems to point toward forbidding the bed.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it said about it? This brings a later statement that limits the source.
They only taught this in the case of. This narrows a ruling.
They know each other, or are familiar with each other

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who is speaking. This rejection does not end the discussion. The very next step answers it with a new distinction, so the bed is not yet forbidden here.

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about this

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chanin bar Ami said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: They only taught this when they do not know each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה — אֲסוּרִים.
phrases.english: but if they know each other, they are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי נָמֵי, מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: And these too, husband and wife, know each other.
phrases.notes: So the guest leniency would not apply to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the guests does not help the couple.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The guest leniency is only for strangers, and a married couple is familiar.

steps.title: Two minds plus a noticeable change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a dressed couple in bed has two minds and also a שינוי, an unusual change that serves as a reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really comparable? There, with the guests, there are two minds but no change. Here, with the couple, there are two minds and also a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the lenient side. The couple's case has an extra protection that familiar guests do not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and cheese on a table look completely normal, so nothing reminds familiar guests to be careful. Sleeping in clothes is unusual, and that oddness itself reminds the couple of the separation. Two minds plus a שינוי is stronger than two minds alone.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? This rejects a comparison.
A change from normal behavior that acts as a reminder

steps.whyThisMatters: The pair of דיעות and שינוי becomes the tool the גמרא uses to answer the next proofs as well.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, there are two minds, but there is no change.
Here, there are two minds and there is also a change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The couple, like familiar guests, would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The couple has two minds and a שינוי, so the guest ruling does not forbid them.

steps.title: Second version: the guest case as proof for forbidding
steps.stepSummary: In another version (איכא דאמרי), the guest case with שמואל's comment is brought directly as a proof that the dressed couple is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: Come and hear. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says two guests may eat at one table, one meat and one cheese. And it was said about this, in the name of שמואל: only when they do not know each other. If they know each other, it is forbidden. And these, husband and wife, know each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same discussion. Here the guest case is used from the start to try to answer the question from step 12 (the איבעיא about a נדה) strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources are the same as in steps 15 to 16, but the order of the argument is different. Here the guest ruling is not a support for leniency. It is an attack: familiar people are forbidden, and a couple is familiar.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing another version of the discussion
Come and hear, introducing a proof
And it was said about it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not new material. It is the same sources arranged as a second version of how the discussion went.

phrases.english: Some say: Come and hear,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָיִים אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Two guests may eat at one table,
this one meat and this one cheese.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And it was said about this: Rav Chanin bar Ami said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: They only taught this when they do not know each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if they know each other, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי נָמֵי, מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה נִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: And these too know each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 15 to 17 as a second version, this time as a direct proof for forbidding.
steps.raayaObject: The dressed couple may not share a bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's guest ruling with שמואל's limitation to strangers.

steps.title: Second version rejected: the couple has a change
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected with the same distinction. The guests have two minds but no change, while the couple has both.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two minds but no change. Here, there are two minds and also a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second-version proof using the דיעות plus שינוי distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since sleeping dressed is unusual, it reminds the couple to be careful. So the strict ruling for familiar guests does not carry over to the couple.

phrases.english: There, there are two minds but there is no change.
Here, there are two minds and there is also a change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The guest proof does not show that the couple is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The couple has a שינוי that familiar guests lack.

steps.title: Proof from the זב and זבה eating together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove the bed is forbidden from our משנה: a זב may not even eat with a זבה, because it could lead them to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A זב may not eat with a זבה, because it may make them used to sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new attempt to answer the question strictly. If even eating together is forbidden for an impure couple, surely sleeping in one bed would be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating together involves two people, so two minds are present, and it is still forbidden. This seems to show that two minds do not protect a couple, even when they are being careful.

keyTerms.meaning: A man impure from an unusual bodily discharge
A woman impure from an unusual flow of blood
Getting used to sin. Closeness that can lead to transgression.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A zav may not eat with a zava
because of becoming accustomed to sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא יֹאכַל הַזָּב עִם הַזָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof for the question of step 12, after the guest proofs were rejected.
steps.raayaObject: A couple in a state of impurity may not be together, even with two minds present.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: לא יאכל הזב עם הזבה.

steps.title: Eating together has no noticeable change
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Eating together has two minds but no שינוי, unlike sleeping dressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, there are two minds but there is no change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the זב and זבה proof with the same distinction as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A couple eating together is ordinary behavior, so nothing unusual reminds them to keep apart. Sleeping in clothes is unusual, so the strict ruling about eating does not prove anything about the dressed couple.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, דֵּיעוֹת אִיכָּא שִׁינּוּי לֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: Here too, there are two minds but there is no change.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, דֵּיעוֹת אִיכָּא שִׁינּוּי לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The זב and זבה proof does not decide the bed case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Eating together lacks a שינוי, while sleeping dressed has one.

steps.title: Proof from a פסוק comparing a נדה to another man's wife
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל lists a נדה next to another man's wife. Just as lying with another man's wife while both are dressed is forbidden, so is lying with one's wife who is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'He did not eat upon the mountains, and he did not raise his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, and he did not defile his neighbor's wife, and he did not come close to a woman who is a נדה.' The פסוק compares a נדה to his neighbor's wife. Just as with his neighbor's wife, lying together while he is in his clothes and she is in hers is forbidden, so too with his wife who is a נדה, lying together while he is in his clothes and she is in hers is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a final proof from a פסוק. It uses an היקש, a comparison of two things placed together in one verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one would allow lying in bed with another man's wife just because both are dressed. Since the פסוק places a נדה right next to her, the same rule applies to one's own wife when she is a נדה. Unlike the earlier proofs, this one cannot be answered with דיעות and שינוי, because the comparison itself forbids the dressed case.

keyTerms.meaning: His neighbor's wife, meaning a married woman
It compares. An היקש links two things placed together in a verse.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"He did not eat upon the mountains

phrases.aramaic: וְעֵינָיו לֹא נָשָׂא אֶל גִּלּוּלֵי בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: and he did not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel
and he did not defile his neighbor's wife
and he did not come near a woman who is a niddah."
It compares a niddah to his neighbor's wife:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ הוּא בְּבִגְדוֹ וְהִיא בְּבִגְדָהּ — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: just as with his neighbor's wife, when he is in his clothes and she is in hers, it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה הוּא בְּבִגְדוֹ וְהִיא בְּבִגְדָהּ — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: so too with his wife who is a niddah, when he is in his clothes and she is in hers, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֶל הֶהָרִים לֹא אָכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof from a פסוק, after the proofs from משניות were rejected.
steps.raayaObject: A husband and his wife who is a נדה may not sleep in one bed, even when both are dressed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The היקש in יחזקאל 18:6 between a נדה and another man's wife.

steps.title: Conclusion: the dressed couple is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof from the פסוק. A נדה and her husband may not sleep in one bed, even when both are dressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question by accepting the last proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs from משניות were all rejected, but the היקש from the פסוק stands. The question from step 12 is settled strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. The proof is accepted.

steps.whatToRemember: Sleeping in one bed with one's wife who is a נדה is forbidden even when both are dressed. This is learned from the היקש to another man's wife, not from the משניות, which were pushed off using the idea of דיעות and שינוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that a husband and wife do not share a bed while she is a נדה.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband and his wife who is a נדה may not sleep in one bed, even when both are dressed.

steps.title: רבי פדת disagrees with the conclusion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the conclusion forbidding a נדה and her husband from sharing a bed while dressed disagrees with רבי פדת. He holds the תורה forbids only closeness that is actual forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי פדת. For רבי פדת said: The תורה forbade only closeness that is actual forbidden relations, as it says: 'Any man to any of his close relatives, do not come near to uncover nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note. The ruling it just reached (no sharing a bed, even dressed) is not accepted by everyone, because רבי פדת holds a more lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת reads 'לא תקרבו' (do not come near) together with 'לגלות ערוה' (to uncover nakedness). In his reading, 'coming near' means the act of relations itself, not hugging or lying together. So when clothing separates them, he sees no prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees; this view argues with another

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is NOT taking back its conclusion here. It is only noting that רבי פדת holds a different opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two ways to read 'לא תקרבו'. One reading forbids only the act itself. The other forbids closeness that could lead to the act. That difference drives the rest of this section.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Pedat:
for Rabbi Pedat said
The Torah did not forbid anything except
closeness that is actual forbidden relations, alone,
phrases.notes: Hugging or lying together dressed is not included in his view.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"Any man, to any of his close relatives,
do not come near to uncover nakedness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:6. The words 'to uncover nakedness' define what 'coming near' means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that an אמורא disagrees with the conclusion of step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי פדת, the תורה forbids only closeness that is actual forbidden relations. Other closeness is not included.

steps.title: עולא kisses his sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that when עולא came home from the study hall, he would kiss his sisters on the chest, or (some say) on the hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came from the house of his teacher, he would kiss his sisters on their chests. Some say: on their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how עולא behaved with his sisters. It shows that he acted with affection and was not worried about forbidden closeness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister is an ערוה, a woman forbidden to him. Yet עולא kissed his sisters out of family affection, not with any desire for relations. His behavior fits the lenient approach of רבי פדת from the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: From the house of his teacher (the study hall)

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא כִּי הָוֵי אָתֵי מִבֵּי רַב
phrases.english: Ulla, when he would come from the house of his teacher,
would kiss his sisters
on their chests,
and some say: on their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא כִּי הָוֵי אָתֵי מִבֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life practice that matches רבי פדת's lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא showed physical affection to his sisters, which suggests he did not treat such closeness as forbidden.

steps.title: עולא's action contradicts his own teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that עולא's practice clashes with his own teaching. He taught that any closeness with a forbidden woman is forbidden, like the saying that a נזיר must keep away from the vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his own action contradicts his own statement. For עולא said: Even any closeness is forbidden, because of the saying: 'Go, go, they tell the נזיר, go around, go around; do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a problem: what עולא did does not match what עולא taught. It simply records the contradiction and moves on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may not eat grapes, so people advise him to stay away from the vineyard altogether. In the same way, עולא taught that one should stay far from any closeness to a forbidden woman. His own kissing of his sisters seems to go against that strict teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Any kind of closeness at all
A נזיר, who is forbidden to eat grapes or wine
Go around, go around (take the long way)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. עולא's TEACHING is strict, like the conclusion in step 23. His PRACTICE was lenient, like רבי פדת. The contradiction is between those two things.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. רבי פדת: the תורה forbids only the act itself. עולא's teaching: stay away from any closeness, just as a נזיר stays away from the vineyard.

phrases.english: And his own [action] contradicts his own [statement],
for Ulla said:
Even any kind of closeness is forbidden,
because of [the saying]: "Go, go, they tell the nazir,
go around, go around; do not come near the vineyard."
phrases.notes: A popular saying: stay far from anything that could lead to a sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares עולא's practice in step 25 with his own strict teaching and finds them in conflict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא taught that any closeness to a forbidden woman is forbidden, so his practice of kissing his sisters contradicts his own teaching.

steps.title: A great student dies young
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from תנא דבי אליהו begins a story about a student who learned a great deal, served Torah scholars, and still died at half his expected lifespan.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of אליהו: There was a story with one student who learned much משנה, read much תנ"ך, and served Torah scholars a great deal. Yet he died at half his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a story from תנא דבי אליהו, that relates to the topic of a נדה. This step sets up the story; its lesson comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story stresses how much this student learned, which makes his early death shocking. That tension sets up the question his wife will ask in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of אליהו (a collection of ברייתות)
Served Torah scholars (learned from them up close)

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Eliyahu:
There was a story with one student
who learned much Mishnah and read much Scripture,
and served Torah scholars a great deal,
and died at half his days.
phrases.notes: He died at about half the normal lifespan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new source, a story connected to how strictly one must separate from a נדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student full of Torah learning died young, which sets up a puzzle about the תורה's promise of long life.

steps.title: The widow challenges the Torah's promise
steps.stepSummary: The student's widow carried his תפילין to shuls and study halls. There she asked: the תורה promises long life, so why did my husband, who learned so much, die young? Her words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife would take his תפילין and carry them around to the shuls and study halls. She said to them: It is written in the תורה, 'For it is your life and the length of your days.' My husband, who learned much and read much...
steps.whatsHappening: The widow publicly challenges the Sages with a פסוק that promises long life to those who learn תורה. This passage ends in the middle of her complaint, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her argument is simple: the פסוק says תורה brings long life, but her husband learned a great deal and died young. This sets up the answer (coming next) that something in his conduct must explain his death.

keyTerms.meaning: The length of your days (long life)

steps.confusionAlert: Her sentence is not finished here. The rest of her complaint, and the answer to it, come on the next amud.

phrases.english: And his wife would take his tefillin
and carry them around to synagogues and study halls,
and she said to them:
It is written in the Torah:
"For it is your life and the length of your days,"
[yet] my husband, who learned much and read much
phrases.notes: Her sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the early death from step 27 into a challenge based on a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תורה's promise of long life in 'כי הוא חייך ואורך ימיך'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her husband learned a great deal of תורה, yet he died young. That seems to contradict the promise of long life.
